row.evidence: ClickTime's pricing page marks SCIM User Provisioning as an Add-on on Starter, Team and Premier, and its SSO guide says SCIM is priced separately from SSO.
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated): SCIM is a separately priced add-on (price not published; contact sales). The help centre says Enterprise plans support SAML and SCIM and SCIM needs SSO set to Allow or Require with Entra, Okta or OneLogin first; the pricing grid shows Okta/OneLogin/Azure AD SSO only on Premier (Custom SAML is an add-on on every tier), so in practice SCIM needs Premier SSO or the Custom SAML add-on plus the SCIM add-on. Prices changed since June: the plan cards now show Starter $15, Team $19, Premier $31 per user/month (June: $12, $15, $27); the page header still says 'Starter plans from $12/user/month' and the billing period is not stated, so the card prices are recorded. Seat caps: Starter up to 25 users, Team and Premier up to 200. Okta OIN app (SAML, SCIM create/update/deactivate); Entra and OneLogin use a generic SCIM app pointed at https://app.clicktime.com/scim. REST API v2 is shown on every plan in the pricing grid but the API Overview article says Team plan or higher.

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: Google SSO included; Okta/OneLogin/Azure AD SSO not included; SCIM and Custom SAML available as paid add-ons.

plans.name: Team
plans.notes: SCIM and Custom SAML available as paid add-ons.

plans.name: Premier
plans.notes: Okta, OneLogin and Azure AD SSO included; SCIM is still an add-on.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Help centre: Enterprise plans support SAML 2.0 and SCIM; SCIM still priced separately (c9).

scim.plan: SCIM User Provisioning add-on (Starter, Team, Premier; Enterprise per help centre)

auth.token_source: Company > Preferences > Security > SCIM > Generate Token (shown once)

operations.notes: Docs say 'attribute updates' without naming PUT or PATCH. OneLogin guide sets the delete action to Suspend.

deprovision.data_retained: User is inactivated; if the user was a timesheet approver, their assignees are reassigned to the first Admin in alphabetical order.

custom.how: ClickTime extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:clicktime:1.0:User (startDate, endDate, role, employmentType, employeeNumber) and urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:clicktimecf:1.0:User:<customFieldName> for person custom fields; admin toggles which fields the IdP manages.

roles.how: role attribute in the ClickTime SCIM extension (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:clicktime:1.0:User:role)

limitations.text: Entra setup uses a non-gallery app with Groups mapping disabled; no group provisioning is documented.
One-way sync: ClickTime does not lock SCIM-managed fields, but edits in ClickTime are overwritten by SCIM.
Requires SSO set to Allow or Require for Entra, Okta or OneLogin before SCIM can be enabled.

capabilities.notes: Deactivate/reactivate via PATCH /Users/{userID} IsActive; role via the Role field; divisions and employment types act as groupings.

endpoints.purpose: Update a User (incl. IsActive, Role, DivisionID)
Get the Users managed by the current user
Update manager permissions for a user
Add Users to an Employment Type
Get custom field definitions for Users

rate_limits.text: 50 requests in 15 seconds (rolling); GET /TimeEntries 10 requests in 5 seconds; page size default 100, max 1000.

okta.notes: OIN page markup checks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate (no Group Push).

entra.notes: Gallery app is SSO only; ClickTime documents SCIM through a non-gallery Entra app.

onelogin.notes: ClickTime's guide uses OneLogin's generic 'SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Core)' app; OneLogin catalogue page not checked (blocks bots).

fallbacks.other_sync: Rippling App Shop integration (provisioning/deactivation and SAML SSO)

conflicts.text: Pricing page header says 'Starter plans from $12/user/month' while the Starter card shows $15 per user/month.
Pricing grid shows REST API on Starter, Team and Premier; the API Overview help article says web services are available on the Team plan or higher.
Pricing grid offers the SCIM add-on on Starter, Team and Premier; the SSO guide says Enterprise plans support SCIM.

open_questions: SCIM add-on price is not published.
Whether SCIM updates use PUT or PATCH, and whether Groups, ServiceProviderConfig or Schemas endpoints exist, is not documented.
Whether SCIM deactivation frees the seat or ends sessions is not documented.
Pricing cards do not state whether $15/$19/$31 are annual or monthly prices.
No Google Workspace provisioning app was checked; Google sign-in is offered but is not SAML.
